    // The number of milliseconds in one day
    const ONE_DAY = 1000 * 60 * 60 * 24;

    // Calculate the difference in milliseconds
    // const differenceMs = Math.abs(secondDate - firstDate);
    const differenceMs = secondDate - firstDate;

    // Convert back to days and return
    const diffDays = Math.round(differenceMs / ONE_DAY);

I have used a few template designs here and there that I have stuck with for years, but recently I decided that I wanted a fresh start and have been over the moon with how my site looks now.” Alexandra Arnold — Photographer “My Format site has been incredibly helpful in sharing my designs, and it’s been the perfect portfolio to highlight my evolving fashion career.” Alexis Walsh — Fashion Designer & Artist “As my artistic practice continues to grow, Format provides me with a seamless platform to showcase my expanding portfolio.” Deshi Deng — Illustrator “I’ve been using format for my photography and filmmaking website since 2015…with all the new features they keep adding, and the option of designing your own custom pages, my website is always evolving.” Rasmus Kaessmann — Photographer & Videographer Start building your dream portfolio commitment-free. See why creatives love Format with a 14 day free trial No credit card required. Get Started Frequently Asked Questions Do I need to know how to code? You absolutely do not need to know how to code to create a professional online portfolio. Your Format site comes with intuitive tools and support from Format Experts that make it easy to customize your site exactly the way you want. Of course, if you want to personalize your website even more, our Pro and Pro Plus plans offer access to CSS and HTML editing. I already have a custom domain. Can I use it with Format? Of course! If you already have a custom domain, you can connect it to your Format website. Our Customer Support team connects user domains to make the process easier. If you’re more hands-on we have  support articles  to get you started, and our Format Experts are available any time you need help. Does Format include hosting for my website? All Format plans automatically include hosting so you don’t need to purchase hosting services through a third party. I’m bad at learning new software, will someone help me? Absolutely! You can get actionable feedback and help with Format Experts. Schedule a one-on-one consultation with our experienced team members to make the most of your portfolio. Format Experts can help you build and optimize a new website or review and make recommendations for your current site—advising on curation, themes and design, SEO, gallery and custom page creation, setting up and selling with your online store, and much more. Are Format sites mobile-ready? Absolutely! All our themes are optimized to be viewed across all devices and platforms: from high-res desktops to laptops and smartphones. Is it easy to use? Yes! Ease of use is our main priority—without sacrificing unique, customizable designs that make your work shine. What makes Format better than what I currently use? We’re a one-stop shop. We have everything you need all in one place: proofing, store, blogging, and beautiful themes to showcase your work. Format also focuses on building the best product for creators like you looking to showcase their work in dynamic and impactful ways. We improve Format on a monthly basis and work hard to have an understanding of what you need in order to succeed. We care about your success. We’re also top rated by  third-party reviews  compared to other website builders on the market. Can I cancel at any time? Absolutely! We would be sad to see you go, but we want you to find the right solution for you. You can reach out to our Customer Success team at any time if something isn’t working and we’ll do our best to solve the issue together. <script type="pmdelayedscript" data-cfasync="false" data-no-optimize="1" data-no-defer="1" data-no-minify="1">
jQuery(document).ready(function($) {
const isSaleLive = true;

if (isSaleLive) {
    const firstDate = new Date();
    firstDate.setHours(0, 0, 0, 0);
    const secondDate = new Date(2023, 11, 15);
//    console.log(`secondDate = ${secondDate}`);

    // The number of milliseconds in one day
    const ONE_DAY = 1000 * 60 * 60 * 24;

    // Calculate the difference in milliseconds
    // const differenceMs = Math.abs(secondDate - firstDate);
    const differenceMs = secondDate - firstDate;

    // Convert back to days and return
    const diffDays = Math.round(differenceMs / ONE_DAY);
    const diffDaysDecimal = Number.parseFloat(differenceMs / ONE_DAY).toFixed(2)
//    console.log("diffDays= " + diffDays);
//    console.log("diffDaysDecimal= " + diffDaysDecimal);
//    console.log("diffDaysDecimal= " + diffDaysDecimal);
    var elem = "";

    const targetDiv = document.getElementById('banner_link');
    const targetDivMobile = document.getElementById('banner_mobile');
    var presale = document.getElementById('presale');
    if (diffDaysDecimal > 1) {
        elem = '<strong>' + diffDays + ' days' + ' left to </strong>';
    }
    if (diffDaysDecimal == 1) {
        elem = '<strong>' + diffDays + ' day' + ' left to </strong>';
    }
    if (diffDaysDecimal == 0) {
        elem = '<strong>Last Chance to </strong>';
    }
    targetDiv.insertAdjacentHTML('afterbegin', elem);
    targetDivMobile.insertAdjacentHTML('afterbegin', elem);
    if(presale) {presale.style.display = "none";}
}
})
</script>

Client Contracts Gallery Password Protection Sign up for a 14 day free trial. No credit card required. Start Building Today Frequently Asked Questions Do I need to know how to code? You absolutely do not need to know how to code to create a professional online portfolio. Your Format site comes with intuitive tools and support from Format Experts that make it easy to customize your site exactly the way you want. Of course, if you want to personalize your website even more, our Pro and Unlimited plans offer access to CSS and HTML editing. I already have a custom domain. Can I use it with Format? Of course! If you already have a custom domain, you can connect it to your Format website. Our Customer Support team connects user domains to make the process easier. If you’re more hands-on we have  support articles  to get you started, and our Format Experts are available any time you need help. Does Format include hosting for my website? All Format plans automatically include hosting so you don’t need to purchase hosting services through a third party. I’m bad at learning new software, will someone help me? Absolutely! You can get actionable feedback and help with Format Experts. Schedule a one-on-one consultation with our experienced team members to make the most of your portfolio. Format Experts can help you build and optimize a new website or review and make recommendations for your current site—advising on curation, themes and design, SEO, gallery and custom page creation, setting up and selling with your online store, and much more. Are Format sites mobile-ready? Absolutely! All our themes are optimized to be viewed across all devices and platforms: from high-res desktops to laptops and smartphones. Is it easy to use? Yes! Ease of use is our main priority—without sacrificing unique, customizable designs that make your work shine. What makes Format better than what I currently use? We’re a one-stop shop. We have everything you need all in one place: proofing, store, blogging, and beautiful themes to showcase your work. Format also focuses on building the best product for creators like you looking to showcase their work in dynamic and impactful ways. We improve Format on a monthly basis and work hard to have an understanding of what you need in order to succeed. We care about your success. We’re also top rated by  third-party reviews  compared to other website builders on the market. Can I cancel at any time? Absolutely! We would be sad to see you go, but we want you to find the right solution for you. You can reach out to our Customer Success team at any time if something isn’t working and we’ll do our best to solve the issue together. <script type="pmdelayedscript" data-cfasync="false" data-no-optimize="1" data-no-defer="1" data-no-minify="1">
jQuery(document).ready(function($) {
const isSaleLive = true;

if (isSaleLive) {
    const firstDate = new Date();
    firstDate.setHours(0, 0, 0, 0);
    const secondDate = new Date(2023, 11, 15);
//    console.log(`secondDate = ${secondDate}`);

    // The number of milliseconds in one day
    const ONE_DAY = 1000 * 60 * 60 * 24;

    // Calculate the difference in milliseconds
    // const differenceMs = Math.abs(secondDate - firstDate);
    const differenceMs = secondDate - firstDate;

    // Convert back to days and return
    const diffDays = Math.round(differenceMs / ONE_DAY);
    const diffDaysDecimal = Number.parseFloat(differenceMs / ONE_DAY).toFixed(2)
//    console.log("diffDays= " + diffDays);
//    console.log("diffDaysDecimal= " + diffDaysDecimal);
//    console.log("diffDaysDecimal= " + diffDaysDecimal);
    var elem = "";

    const targetDiv = document.getElementById('banner_link');
    const targetDivMobile = document.getElementById('banner_mobile');
    var presale = document.getElementById('presale');
    if (diffDaysDecimal > 1) {
        elem = '<strong>' + diffDays + ' days' + ' left to </strong>';
    }
    if (diffDaysDecimal == 1) {
        elem = '<strong>' + diffDays + ' day' + ' left to </strong>';
    }
    if (diffDaysDecimal == 0) {
        elem = '<strong>Last Chance to </strong>';
    }
    targetDiv.insertAdjacentHTML('afterbegin', elem);
    targetDivMobile.insertAdjacentHTML('afterbegin', elem);
    if(presale) {presale.style.display = "none";}
}
})
</script>

<h1 class="kt-adv-heading11423_a9a7e9-b6 hero__title header-a3z6jyknxl7j874qa _a3z6jyknxl7j874pb hero__titlehero__text-eyebrow paragraph-a3z6jyknxl7j874fx wp-block-kadence-advancedheading" data-kb-block="kb-adv-heading11423_a9a7e9-b6">Our passion.<br>Our purpose.<br>Our team.</h1>
</div></div>



<div class="wp-block-kadence-column kadence-column11423_e5edb3-3a inner-column-2"><div class="kt-inside-inner-col">
<p class="kt-adv-heading11423_5f7b34-53 hero__cta-blurb wp-block-kadence-advancedheading" data-kb-block="kb-adv-heading11423_5f7b34-53">We are Format — a team of experts at the intersection of the tech and creative spaces. We’re driven by a singular passion and purpose: to help photographers succeed and thrive.</p>



<p class="kt-adv-heading11423_b76299-83 hero__cta-blurb wp-block-kadence-advancedheading" data-kb-block="kb-adv-heading11423_b76299-83">We are passionate about finding new ways to provide the photography community the tools and resources they need to share their work and grow their business. Our work is never done.</p>
</div></div>

</div></div>

</div></div>

These values guide who we are and how we work.</p>

</div></div>

<p class="kt-adv-heading11423_4644c7-cd wp-block-kadence-advancedheading" data-kb-block="kb-adv-heading11423_4644c7-cd">Our vision and how we work provides our team members with the freedom and resources needed to work creatively and meet personal and professional goals.</p>

<p class="kt-adv-heading11423_a13ffd-6b wp-block-kadence-advancedheading" data-kb-block="kb-adv-heading11423_a13ffd-6b">No matter which department, title, or role you have at Format, we all are unified by the same goal: empowering the freedom of professional photographers. <span class="kt-adv-heading11423_890238-a9 box-title wp-block-kadence-advancedheading" data-kb-block="kb-adv-heading11423_890238-a9">We are goal driven.</span>



<p class="kt-adv-heading11423_b0d156-7f wp-block-kadence-advancedheading" data-kb-block="kb-adv-heading11423_b0d156-7f">Our goals are big—for both our business and ourselves. </div></div></div></div>

<p class="kt-adv-heading11423_5ba4e1-84 wp-block-kadence-advancedheading" data-kb-block="kb-adv-heading11423_5ba4e1-84">On <strong>November 11, 2021</strong>, Format announced that they are joining forces with Zenfolio. The coming together of two market leaders in providing services to photographers is a significant shift in direction for the industry.</p>
</div></div>

</div></div></div></div>

<p class="kt-adv-heading11423_25eaee-fe wp-block-kadence-advancedheading" data-kb-block="kb-adv-heading11423_25eaee-fe">We trust in the talents of our team. We hire driven people and give everyone the autonomy they need to be successful.</p>

<p class="kt-adv-heading11423_db2d23-14 wp-block-kadence-advancedheading" data-kb-block="kb-adv-heading11423_db2d23-14">Working with the creative community, it’s no wonder why we’re driven to deliver beautiful design that honors the quality of our members’ work. We believe in building an inclusive work environment that fosters innovation, creativity, and diversity.</p>

Our purpose. Our team. We are Format — a team of experts at the intersection of the tech and creative spaces. We’re driven by a singular passion and purpose: to help photographers succeed and thrive. We are passionate about finding new ways to provide the photography community the tools and resources they need to share their work and grow their business. Our work is never done. Born from creativity. Shaped by our values. We are a company built on the things we believe in — impact, trust, care, simplicity, and a healthy dose of hard work. These values guide who we are and how we work. Let’s get social. Get an unfiltered view of life at Format. Follow @useformat View Page How we work sets us apart. Our vision and how we work provides our team members with the freedom and resources needed to work creatively and meet personal and professional goals. One team, one goal. No matter which department, title, or role you have at Format, we all are unified by the same goal: empowering the freedom of professional photographers. While each of us has a different responsibility in that process, it all comes back to that shared purpose. We are goal driven. Our goals are big—for both our business and ourselves. That’s why we set professional and personal goals and check in each quarter to ensure we’re on track to meet them. This helps build a culture of focus, accountability, and success. Bootstrapped since day one. On  November 11, 2021 , Format announced that they are joining forces with Zenfolio. The coming together of two market leaders in providing services to photographers is a significant shift in direction for the industry. Autonomy to succeed. We trust in the talents of our team. And by doing so, give them the freedom to get things done. More than that, our team members make important decisions every day and have a tangible impact on the business. We hire driven people and give everyone the autonomy they need to be successful. Design focused. Working with the creative community, it’s no wonder why we’re driven to deliver beautiful design that honors the quality of our members’ work. Our standard for great design is high and it informs everything we do. Authentic culture. There are a lot of reasons our team members love working at Format, but being able to bring their true selves to work each and every day is at the top of the list. We believe in building an inclusive work environment that fosters innovation, creativity, and diversity. Like what you hear? <script type="pmdelayedscript" data-cfasync="false" data-no-optimize="1" data-no-defer="1" data-no-minify="1">
jQuery(document).ready(function($) {
const isSaleLive = true;

if (isSaleLive) {
    const firstDate = new Date();
    firstDate.setHours(0, 0, 0, 0);
    const secondDate = new Date(2023, 11, 15);
//    console.log(`secondDate = ${secondDate}`);

    // The number of milliseconds in one day
    const ONE_DAY = 1000 * 60 * 60 * 24;

    // Calculate the difference in milliseconds
    // const differenceMs = Math.abs(secondDate - firstDate);
    const differenceMs = secondDate - firstDate;

    // Convert back to days and return
    const diffDays = Math.round(differenceMs / ONE_DAY);
    const diffDaysDecimal = Number.parseFloat(differenceMs / ONE_DAY).toFixed(2)
//    console.log("diffDays= " + diffDays);
//    console.log("diffDaysDecimal= " + diffDaysDecimal);
//    console.log("diffDaysDecimal= " + diffDaysDecimal);
    var elem = "";

    const targetDiv = document.getElementById('banner_link');
    const targetDivMobile = document.getElementById('banner_mobile');
    var presale = document.getElementById('presale');
    if (diffDaysDecimal > 1) {
        elem = '<strong>' + diffDays + ' days' + ' left to </strong>';
    }
    if (diffDaysDecimal == 1) {
        elem = '<strong>' + diffDays + ' day' + ' left to </strong>';
    }
    if (diffDaysDecimal == 0) {
        elem = '<strong>Last Chance to </strong>';
    }
    targetDiv.insertAdjacentHTML('afterbegin', elem);
    targetDivMobile.insertAdjacentHTML('afterbegin', elem);
    if(presale) {presale.style.display = "none";}
}
})
</script>

//    console.log("diffDaysDecimal= " + diffDaysDecimal);
//    console.log("diffDaysDecimal= " + diffDaysDecimal);
    var elem = "";

    const targetDiv = document.getElementById('banner_link');
    const targetDivMobile = document.getElementById('banner_mobile');
    var presale = document.getElementById('presale');
    if (diffDaysDecimal > 1) {
        elem = '<strong>' + diffDays + ' days' + ' left to </strong>';
    }
    if (diffDaysDecimal == 1) {
        elem = '<strong>' + diffDays + ' day' + ' left to </strong>';
    }
    if (diffDaysDecimal == 0) {
        elem = '<strong>Last Chance to </strong>';
    }
    targetDiv.insertAdjacentHTML('afterbegin', elem);
    targetDivMobile.insertAdjacentHTML('afterbegin', elem);
    if(presale) {presale.style.display = "none";}
}
})

	<div class="entry-content">
		
<p class="wp-block-paragraph">This month’s Member Milestones spans public art, photojournalism, and illustration—three artists whose work is landing in front of new audiences right now. A double-exposed photograph becomes a public art installation. A year-long documentary project earns a place in The New York Times. A three-year archive of sketchbooks debuts as an artbook at Prairie Comics Fest. Here’s a closer look at the vision and cultural impact behind each one.</p>



<p class="wp-block-paragraph">Format has always believed that a platform is only as powerful as the people who call it home. This month, we’re reminded why that belief holds—three extraordinary artists are making their mark on the creative world, and we couldn’t be prouder to be the place they choose to share their work.</p>

<h2 class="wp-block-heading"><strong>Jenna FitzGerald’s Double-Exposed Photography Goes Public at Artscape Youngplace</strong></h2>



<p class="wp-block-paragraph"><a href="https://jennafitzgerald.format.com" target="_blank">Jenna FitzGerald’s</a> double-exposed 35mm photograph is now installed on a billboard at 180 Shaw Street, outside Artscape Youngplace, on view through the end of September as part of the Critical Distance Centre for Curators’ public art program.</p>



<p class="wp-block-paragraph">The Toronto multidisciplinary artist works at the intersection of technology and nature, moving between photography, web design, and 3D modelling. This piece layers a blue picnic blanket covered in foraged mushrooms—shot on a group hike outside Toronto with fellow OCAD students and fungi guides—over two frames taken in Mexico City: a skyward shot of a lamp fixture and a view of the courtyard at the Museum of Anthropology. The blanket appears to float, suspended between two cities and two ways of seeing. Writer Annapoorane Rajagopal Valarmathy penned an <a href="https://criticaldistance.ca/assets/2026/08/JFIT-OCAD_Billboard_Essay-by-Annapoorane-Rajagopal-Valarmathy_layout.pdf" target="_blank">accompanying essay</a> for the installation.</p>



<p class="wp-block-paragraph">On her Format portfolio, built on the <a href="https://www.format.com/website-templates/grace" target="_blank">Grace theme</a>, FitzGerald organizes her work by medium—letting photography, web design, and 3D work each hold their own space. It’s a fitting counterpart to a piece built on layering different tools and materials.</p>

<h2 class="wp-block-heading"><strong>Paola Chapdelaine’s Yearlong Scouting Project Lands in The New York Times</strong></h2>



<p class="wp-block-paragraph"><a href="https://www.paolachapdelaine.com/" target="_blank">Paola Chapdelaine’s</a> photographs from her yearlong documentary project, <em>Troop 163</em>, are featured in The New York Times Opinion section, in the article “<a href="https://www.nytimes.com/2026/07/25/opinion/boy-scouts-girls-gender.html" target="_blank">When Girls Get to Be Boy Scouts</a>.”</p>



<p class="wp-block-paragraph">The French photojournalist and documentary photographer is based in the New York area and a member of Women Photograph and NPPA. With a background in political science and urban development, she moved into photojournalism in 2020 and received the Director’s Fellowship from the Documentary Practice & Visual Journalism program at the International Center of Photography. Her reporting spans social and political issues across the United States—youth in the digital age, community violence intervention, the American political divide—and climate stories like the aftermath of Hurricane Helene in North Carolina, with work in The New York Times, The Washington Post, New York Magazine, The Wall Street Journal, The New Republic, NBC, Politico, and The Guardian.</p>



<p class="wp-block-paragraph">In March 2025, Chapdelaine began documenting Troop 163, the all-girl Boy Scout troop of Closter, New Jersey—part of Scouting America since the organization opened to girls in 2017. She followed the troop through weekly meetings, excursions, and merit badge requirements, and was eventually invited by Scoutmaster Dr. Song to teach the girls the Photography merit badge herself. The featured image captures Jemima and Evelyn at a Court of Honor on September 27, 2025, as they became the troop’s first two female Eagle Scouts. Chapdelaine plans to keep following the troop.</p>



<p class="wp-block-paragraph">Her Format portfolio, built on the <a href="https://www.format.com/website-templates/horizon-left" target="_blank">Horizon Left</a> theme, gives visitors room to move through her strongest images at their own pace, with captions adding context along the way—a pace that suits a project built over more than a year of earned trust.</p>

<h2 class="wp-block-heading"><strong>Wenting Li Turns Three Years of Sketchbooks Into an Artbook at Prairie Comics Fest</strong></h2>



<p class="wp-block-paragraph"><a href="https://wentingli.com" target="_blank">Wenting Li’s</a> new artbook, <em>memory ~ archive</em>, exhibits at Prairie Comics Fest in Winnipeg this September—three years of drawings and comics distilled from seven sketchbooks into a single zine.</p>



<p class="wp-block-paragraph">The illustrator is based in Tkaronto’s west end by way of Chengdu, China—never not drawing, never not observing the world around them. Working across print and digital publication, drawing and painting, installation, comics, and murals, their practice moves through recurring questions: how to read a landscape, the nature of data storage and digital garbage, communally possible futures, collecting, drawing from memory, and specificity in how stories get told.</p>



<p class="wp-block-paragraph">The sketchbooks were carried between southwestern Ontario and Hong Kong, Macau, and mainland China. Working from both observation and memory over that span, Wenting lets the line between what’s remembered and what’s imagined become a shifting marker—asking, in effect, what the real distance is between memory and archive. The exhibition runs September 5-6 at the Manitoba Museum for Prairie Comics Fest.</p>



<p class="wp-block-paragraph">Wenting’s Format portfolio, built on the <a href="https://www.format.com/website-templates/amazon" target="_blank">Amazon theme</a>, puts the full colourful range of their practice on display right on the home page—a fitting echo of <em>memory ~ archive</em> itself, which pulls years of sketchbooks spanning multiple mediums into one place without flattening what made each one distinct.</p>

<h2 class="wp-block-heading"><strong>Why These Portfolios Matter</strong></h2>



<p class="wp-block-paragraph">Every member featured this month is doing something that goes beyond technique or aesthetics. They are using their practice to document communities, hold public space, and preserve memory in ways that outlast any single project or exhibition.</p>



<p class="wp-block-paragraph">That’s what a portfolio is at its best: not just a collection of work, but a visual calling card that tells the world who you are and what you stand for.</p>

Sarah Jasmine August 27, 2026 Share this article This month’s Member Milestones spans public art, photojournalism, and illustration—three artists whose work is landing in front of new audiences right now. A double-exposed photograph becomes a public art installation. A year-long documentary project earns a place in The New York Times. A three-year archive of sketchbooks debuts as an artbook at Prairie Comics Fest. Here’s a closer look at the vision and cultural impact behind each one. Format has always believed that a platform is only as powerful as the people who call it home. This month, we’re reminded why that belief holds—three extraordinary artists are making their mark on the creative world, and we couldn’t be prouder to be the place they choose to share their work. Table of Contents Jenna FitzGerald's Double-Exposed Photography Goes Public at Artscape Youngplace Paola Chapdelaine's Yearlong Scouting Project Lands in The New York Times Wenting Li Turns Three Years of Sketchbooks Into an Artbook at Prairie Comics Fest Why These Portfolios Matter Got a Milestone Worth Celebrating? Jenna FitzGerald’s Double-Exposed Photography Goes Public at Artscape Youngplace Jenna FitzGerald’s double-exposed 35mm photograph is now installed on a billboard at 180 Shaw Street, outside Artscape Youngplace, on view through the end of September as part of the Critical Distance Centre for Curators’ public art program. The Toronto multidisciplinary artist works at the intersection of technology and nature, moving between photography, web design, and 3D modelling. This piece layers a blue picnic blanket covered in foraged mushrooms—shot on a group hike outside Toronto with fellow OCAD students and fungi guides—over two frames taken in Mexico City: a skyward shot of a lamp fixture and a view of the courtyard at the Museum of Anthropology. The blanket appears to float, suspended between two cities and two ways of seeing. Writer Annapoorane Rajagopal Valarmathy penned an accompanying essay for the installation. On her Format portfolio, built on the Grace theme , FitzGerald organizes her work by medium—letting photography, web design, and 3D work each hold their own space. It’s a fitting counterpart to a piece built on layering different tools and materials. Jenna FitzGerald, foraging , 2024, double-exposed film, digital scan. Image courtesy of the artist. Paola Chapdelaine’s Yearlong Scouting Project Lands in The New York Times Paola Chapdelaine’s photographs from her yearlong documentary project, Troop 163 , are featured in The New York Times Opinion section, in the article “ When Girls Get to Be Boy Scouts .” The French photojournalist and documentary photographer is based in the New York area and a member of Women Photograph and NPPA. With a background in political science and urban development, she moved into photojournalism in 2020 and received the Director’s Fellowship from the Documentary Practice & Visual Journalism program at the International Center of Photography. Her reporting spans social and political issues across the United States—youth in the digital age, community violence intervention, the American political divide—and climate stories like the aftermath of Hurricane Helene in North Carolina, with work in The New York Times, The Washington Post, New York Magazine, The Wall Street Journal, The New Republic, NBC, Politico, and The Guardian. In March 2025, Chapdelaine began documenting Troop 163, the all-girl Boy Scout troop of Closter, New Jersey—part of Scouting America since the organization opened to girls in 2017. She followed the troop through weekly meetings, excursions, and merit badge requirements, and was eventually invited by Scoutmaster Dr. Song to teach the girls the Photography merit badge herself. The featured image captures Jemima and Evelyn at a Court of Honor on September 27, 2025, as they became the troop’s first two female Eagle Scouts. Chapdelaine plans to keep following the troop. Her Format portfolio, built on the Horizon Left theme, gives visitors room to move through her strongest images at their own pace, with captions adding context along the way—a pace that suits a project built over more than a year of earned trust. Paola Chapdelaine, Troop 163 , 2025. Zoe, a member of Scout Troop 163, plays at the bottom of the pool after completing swimming requirements, June 2, 2025, Closter, NJ. Image courtesy of the artist. Wenting Li Turns Three Years of Sketchbooks Into an Artbook at Prairie Comics Fest Wenting Li’s new artbook, memory ~ archive , exhibits at Prairie Comics Fest in Winnipeg this September—three years of drawings and comics distilled from seven sketchbooks into a single zine. The illustrator is based in Tkaronto’s west end by way of Chengdu, China—never not drawing, never not observing the world around them. Working across print and digital publication, drawing and painting, installation, comics, and murals, their practice moves through recurring questions: how to read a landscape, the nature of data storage and digital garbage, communally possible futures, collecting, drawing from memory, and specificity in how stories get told. The sketchbooks were carried between southwestern Ontario and Hong Kong, Macau, and mainland China. Working from both observation and memory over that span, Wenting lets the line between what’s remembered and what’s imagined become a shifting marker—asking, in effect, what the real distance is between memory and archive. The exhibition runs September 5-6 at the Manitoba Museum for Prairie Comics Fest. Wenting’s Format portfolio, built on the Amazon theme , puts the full colourful range of their practice on display right on the home page—a fitting echo of memory ~ archive itself, which pulls years of sketchbooks spanning multiple mediums into one place without flattening what made each one distinct. Wenting Li, memory ~ archive , 2026. Video by the artist. Why These Portfolios Matter Every member featured this month is doing something that goes beyond technique or aesthetics. They are using their practice to document communities, hold public space, and preserve memory in ways that outlast any single project or exhibition. That’s what a portfolio is at its best: not just a collection of work, but a visual calling card that tells the world who you are and what you stand for. Your work deserves the same intentionality.
